results.detail: NOT GUARANTEED, measured: after their own drivers ran, world A reads integrity=Low policies=[NO_WRITE_UP] and world B reads integrity=Low policies=[NO_WRITE_UP]. Each worker's own workspace write grant is the LAST writer of its world's label, so NO_READ_UP is replaced by NO_WRITE_UP while that worker runs. A third worker can therefore read both worlds by running raw code. The model-visible route stays closed — the guard denies read/grep/glob on those paths regardless of any label — so what is lost is isolation from ARBITRARY RAW CODE between concurrently active worlds, not the confidentiality of data at rest or the tool surface.
